def max_profit(prices, k):
    if not prices:
        return 0
    
    n = len(prices)
    
    # If we have more transactions than days, we can simply make a transaction on each day.
    if k >= n / 2:
        return sum(b - a for a, b in zip(prices[:-1], prices[1:]))
    
    # dp[i][j] := max profit up until prices[j] using at most i transactions. We use one extra element to simplify edge cases.
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(k + 1)]
    
    # Initialize max profit up until day j using 0 transactions.
    for i in range(k + 1):
        dp[i][0] = 0
    
    # Initialize max profit with 1 transaction using 0 elements.
    for j in range(n + 1):
        dp[0][j] = 0
    
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        # Track the max profit we can get by selling on day j.
        max_profit_sell_on_day = float('-inf')
        
        for j in range(1, n + 1):
            # Track the max profit we can get by buying on day j.
            max_profit_buy_on_day = dp[i - 1][j - 1]
            
            # We can only buy before we sell.
            max_profit_buy_on_day = max(max_profit_buy_on_day, dp[i][j - 1])
            
            # Track the max profit we can get by selling on day j.
            max_profit_sell_on_day = max(max_profit_sell_on_day, prices[j - 1] + max_profit_buy_on_day)
            
            # Update the max profit up until day j using i transactions.
            dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j - 1], max_profit_sell_on_day)
            
    return dp[k][n]

        # Check if x is present at mid
        if arr[mid] < x:
            low = mid + 1
 
        # If x is greater, ignore left half
